# CC0 inline-four proxy bank

This runtime bank is derived from two CC0 field recordings. It may be copied,
modified and redistributed without attribution. Attribution and precise source
identity are retained here anyway so future vehicle authors can audit what they
are hearing.

Engine loops:

- Author: TheLittleCrow
- Title: `Car Engine Contact Recording-Mini Cooper S 2019.wav`
- Source: https://freesound.org/people/TheLittleCrow/sounds/669618/
- License: Creative Commons 0
- Downloaded artifact: Freesound HQ OGG preview, 48 kHz stereo
- SHA-256: `5F23A1FD37ED9D0E1EDBB6D4D533DB9B0C2B2181239B225FBAD0CD1BC9CF9AE7`
- Processing: the synchronized chassis and engine-block contact channels were
  mixed 68/32, split into seven steady or slowly changing engine-order regions,
  DC corrected, periodically equalized, seam crossfaded and peak-safe
  normalized. No synthetic pitch change was baked in. The 1,650 RPM band uses
  the recording's final stable idle-to-low-RPM plateau instead of the previous
  falling sweep, avoiding an audible electronic warble.

Startup:

- Author: sound_catcher99
- Title: `Fiat Punto Grande - starting up, running and turning off.wav`
- Source: https://freesound.org/people/sound_catcher99/sounds/425158/
- License: Creative Commons 0
- Downloaded artifact: Freesound HQ OGG preview, 96 kHz mono
- SHA-256: `EA23ED5614D95F9D66BE089DDCFAAA7264DBCCCD8932B4FF5E4C060ACF8C14EE`
- Processing: first 5.5 seconds, DC corrected, short edge ramps and peak-safe
  normalization.

This is a real-engine development proxy, not a recording of a Peugeot 206 RC
or its EW10J4S engine. Replace it with a measured Peugeot multi-perspective RPM
bank when one can be recorded or licensed.
